clue.text: Constant area for one to circulate in prison

parts.note: C is the usual symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

indicators.note: to circulate here means to turn round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: for one, i.e. for example, is EG (exempli gratia)

explanation.surface: A cell or yard inside a jail where an inmate is allowed to walk around.
explanation.definitionFit: A cage is an enclosure for confining captives, so it serves as a synonym for a jail.

clue.text: Project a gentle touch within religious group

indicators.note: within puts the first pieces inside the word that follows

parts.note: a cult is a religious group
a tap is a gentle touch

explanation.surface: A soft pat given inside a religious sect.
explanation.definitionFit: To catapult is to project or hurl something forcefully, as the siege machine throws stones.

clue.text: Upright piano in part of India misplaced

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast

indicators.note: in puts the music letter inside the word for misplaced

parts.note: something misplaced is lost
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly

explanation.surface: An upright piano has gone missing somewhere in a region of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright piano' reads as a single instrument, but 'Upright' is the definition and 'piano' only gives P.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalpost is one of the two vertical posts of a goal, an upright in sporting language.

clue.text: The clan is excited about daughter of the northern isles

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the daughter
excited letters are stirred up, so the words the clan is get rearranged

parts.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A Scottish family gets worked up about one of its daughters from the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges THE CLAN IS into SHETLANIC, and 'about' puts it around D. The Shetland Islands lie north of mainland Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Shetlandic is the adjective, and also the dialect, belonging to Shetland, the island group far to Scotland's north.

clue.text: Mostly very good about limitations of the accommodation

indicators.note: about means around, so the shortened word surrounds the other letters
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: holy means saintly, extremely good

indicators.note: the limitations of a word are its outer edges, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: The accommodation is nearly excellent, apart from its limitations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' leaves HOL, and 'about' puts it around TE, the edges of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is a building providing rooms for travellers, so it is a place of accommodation.

clue.text: Watch report of herb superior to rest?

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: thyme is a herb and peace is rest; in a down clue superior to puts the herb above the rest, giving THYME PEACE

explanation.surface: A gardener asks whether one herb outranks all the others.
explanation.walkthrough: THYME PEACE said aloud sounds like TIME PIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: A timepiece is any clock or instrument for telling the time, of which a wristwatch is one kind.

clue.text: Observer overlooked what another type of paper would catch?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a watcher who sees everything without being noticed

definitions.text: what another type of paper would catch?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: flypaper catches flies, so wallpaper, another paper, would catch one on the wall

explanation.walkthrough: 'Observer' and 'paper' together suggest the Observer newspaper; the paper is wallpaper set against flypaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an unseen witness to private events, like an insect sitting unnoticed on a wall.

clue.text: International in time becomes choice

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the word for time

parts.note: a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A player's international cap is the choice of the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Choice as an adjective means fine and select, as dainty morsels are delicate and of high quality.

clue.text: Stop using campaign item about Republican rumour

parts.note: to can something is to stop using or scrap it

indicators.note: about means around, so the advertisement goes around the party letter

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is an item in a marketing or political campaign

explanation.surface: A campaign advert about a Republican is pulled because it spreads a false story.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is an unfounded story or false report, a rumour put about to mislead.

clue.text: Passage was published, second one to appear in Times?

indicators.note: to appear in something is to be inside it, so these pieces go between the outer letters

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, so Times gives two of them, TT
a story that was published ran in the paper
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A newspaper item ran, and a second one is due to appear in The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to appear in' puts RAN, S and I between the two Ts. Times as a plural gives T twice, not the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the act of passing through or across, the same as a passage from one place to another.

clue.text: Being unappreciative about holiday illumination

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes around the second

parts.note: slighting means treating with disdain, being unappreciative
a trip is a holiday or excursion

explanation.surface: Someone ungrateful moans about the holiday lights.
explanation.walkthrough: SLIGHTING goes around TRIP, which sits after its first letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: Strip lighting is lighting from long fluorescent tubes, a form of illumination in offices and kitchens.

clue.text: India invested in factory working to get quantity of money?

indicators.note: money invested in a business is put into it, so one letter goes inside the others

parts.note: a mill is a factory, such as a cotton mill
a machine that is working is on
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An Indian buyer puts money into a factory that is running, hoping to make a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A million is a number, and the question mark admits it is usually a sum of pounds or dollars only by implication.

clue.text: Conference item to be delivered with speed? This should fix your notes

parts.note: academics deliver a paper at a conference
clip means speed, as in going at a fair clip

explanation.surface: A speaker hurries to deliver a talk at a conference, clutching the notes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description rather than a synonym: notes here are sheets of paper held together.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper clip is a bent wire fastener for holding sheets together, so it would fasten your loose notes.

clue.text: Aquatic mammal showing excessive energy beside river

parts.note: OTT is over the top, i.e. excessive
E is the physics symbol for energy
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A water creature shows tremendous energy playing on the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter is a fish-eating member of the weasel family that lives in and by rivers.

clue.text: Street right through area of land — unknown quantity — it may never be restored

indicators.note: going through something places it in the middle, so these letters sit inside the others

parts.note: a lot is a plot or area of land
ST is the address abbreviation for street
proper means right or correct
Y is one of the letters used in algebra for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A road runs right through someone's land, a stretch of unknown size that may never be given back.
explanation.definitionFit: Lost property is items mislaid by their owners and handed in, which may never be reclaimed.

clue.text: Distinguished fellow initially obtained two degrees? Not seen around university

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word obtained

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity and MA is Master of Arts, two university degrees

indicators.note: the negative word goes around the abbreviation for university

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A notable academic got two degrees, yet is never seen on campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distinguished' means set apart from the rest here, not eminent.
explanation.definitionFit: The odd man out is the one person who differs from the others in a group, distinguished in the sense of marked out.

clue.text: Cosmetic comments that are impertinent don't go away

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk, impertinent remarks
to stick is to stay put, not go away

explanation.surface: Cheeky remarks about make-up that refuse to fade.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipstick is a coloured cosmetic applied to the lips, a staple of make-up.

clue.text: Drunk comes round not quite roaring early in the evening

indicators.note: the first word wraps around the next pieces

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk

indicators.note: not quite drops the final letter

parts.note: wild means roaring or unrestrained, as in a roaring party

explanation.surface: A drunk comes to after a wild night that began at dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' cuts WILD to WIL, and 'comes round' puts TIGHT around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is the dim light just after sunset, the start of evening, so it works for the phrase of time.

clue.text: Oversight from treating things as a lark for example?

definitions.text: Oversight from treating things as a lark for example?

parts.words: Oversight from treating things as a lark for example?
parts.note: a lark is a bird, so seeing things as one would means looking down on them from the sky

explanation.walkthrough: 'treating things as a lark' suggests not taking them seriously, but the lark is the bird, and the oversight is a view over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A view from high above, as a flying bird would see it, gives a panoramic overview of a scene.

clue.text: Work in malicious gossip, reversing support for paparazzo?

indicators.note: reversing turns the whole assembly round, reading it from the end
in places the work inside the gossip word

parts.note: dirt is scandalous or malicious gossip
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A tabloid photographer does work digging up scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts OP inside DIRT to give DOPIRT, and 'reversing' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripod is a three-legged stand that holds a camera steady, used by press photographers.

clue.text: Pretend to agree with expression of doubt, filling time

indicators.note: filling something means going inside it

parts.note: an hour is a period of time
um is a hesitant sound expressing doubt

explanation.surface: Someone humours a speaker, saying 'um' to fill the gaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To humour someone is to go along with their wishes or ideas to keep them happy.

clue.text: Depression, after initially fading, is difficult

indicators.note: the word's first letter has faded away, so its opening letter goes

parts.note: a trough is a depression, in the ground or in a weather chart

explanation.surface: A weather low, once it begins to fade, still makes for hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough time or rough journey is a hard one, so the adjective means difficult.

clue.text: Job assessment? Shock to receive extra pay cut

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it in, so the second part goes inside the first

parts.note: to appal is to shock

indicators.note: cut here means shortened, losing its last letter

parts.note: a raise is an increase in pay

explanation.surface: An employee's annual review brings the shock of a pay rise being cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' takes the last letter off RAISE, leaving RAIS, which goes inside APPAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraisal is a formal review of an employee's performance, the assessment of how someone does their job.

clue.text: Might at last trap someone in red?

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of the word trap

parts.note: to be in the red is to be in debt, so such a person owes money: an ower

explanation.surface: A trap is finally sprung on someone deep in debt, showing who holds the might.
explanation.definitionFit: Power and might both mean strength or force, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Most of confirmation about volume is stipulation

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened word goes around the rest
most of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: proof is confirmation that something is true

explanation.surface: Nearly all the confirmation of the amount turns out to be a condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' turns PROOF into PROO, and 'about' puts it around V and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a condition attached to an agreement, a clause that stipulates something.

clue.text: Keen political faction suppressing misfortune

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down or holding in, so one word contains the other

parts.note: a wing is a faction of a political party, such as the left wing
ill means misfortune or harm, as in ill befell him

explanation.surface: An eager party group hushes up a run of bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Willing means ready and eager to do something, so it is a synonym of keen.

clue.text: Brutally treated after backsliding, a politician offering insults

indicators.note: after sliding backwards the word runs from right to left

parts.note: gored means wounded by horns, i.e. brutally treated
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician who has been savagely handled after slipping back in the polls hurls insults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after backsliding' reverses GORED to give DEROG, then A and TORY follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Derogatory remarks belittle someone, so they are disparaging, offering insults.

clue.text: Unfunded, missing new part of comedy show

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the named letter is dropped

parts.note: skint is British slang for having no money

explanation.surface: A comedy show with no money and no new material.
explanation.walkthrough: Skint is British slang for broke.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch, one item in a revue or comedy programme.
